_doc: Slug -> the OBSERVED-WEATHER pressure signal at the ingredient's real import-origin growing region. For import-dominated produce, a representative NOAA GHCN-Daily station in the origin's growing belt gives a graded frost/heat read (TMIN/TMAX) at the place the Census import-origin concentration already names we depend on — the corpus's biggest pressure blind spot (US-only USDM/NWS cannot reach Michoacan or Sinaloa). For tropical/Pacific ocean-sourced items where a land-station frost read is meaningless, the honest signal is the CPC ONI (El Nino/La Nina regime) instead.
_source: NOAA NCEI GHCN-Daily per-station CSV (ncei.noaa.gov/data/global-historical-climatology-network-daily/access/<STATION>.csv; TMIN/TMAX/PRCP in tenths, divide by 10) + NOAA CPC ONI (cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/data/indices/oni.ascii.txt). Both keyless, US-gov public domain, redistributable. Fetch runs on the operator's Mac.
_signal_split: land = observed weather at a growing-region station (frost/heat) — for subtropical produce whose supply a cold snap or heat wave at the origin actually moves. oni = the ENSO regime gauge — for Pacific/tropical items (Ecuador/Chile shrimp+salmon aquaculture, tropical fruit) where a single land station is not the driver. Atlantic-Canada wild seafood (lobster/crab/halibut/clams) and temperate produce (Canadian beet) get NEITHER here — their supply is quota/stock-driven (NOAA landings, pending) — an honest absence.
_status: V1, GROUNDED STATIONS (each verified recent: TMIN through 2025-26) but crop->region assignments NEED CALIBRATION. A station is a REGIONAL PROXY for the origin growing belt, not the exact farm. The whole layer is HELD-UNTIL-CALIBRATED per ADR-013/014: present-direction only, never a forecast, never a magnitude, never touching the measured price band, and it does not ship 'proven' until data/pressure-calibration.json backs each contributor (incl. the feed-complex double-count guard before any NASS corn/soy CONDITION is stacked on the existing feed proxies).

mx-sinaloa.note: Culiacan / Sinaloa winter-vegetable export belt (warm-season fruiting veg)

mx-michoacan.note: Morelia + Zamora, Michoacan — avocado, lime, citrus, berry

mx-baja.note: Mexicali / Baja California (cool-season greens, brassicas, herbs, roots; some tomato/berry)

mx-bajio.note: Guanajuato / Queretaro / Jalisco Bajio berry + veg belt

pe-coast.note: Peru central coast (blueberry) — refine toward Ica / La Libertad on calibration

habanero-pepper.note: also Yucatan; Sinaloa proxy for now

shrimp.note: Ecuador Pacific aquaculture — ENSO regime, not a land station

_deliberately_absent.whole-lobster / whole-crab / whole-halib: Atlantic-Canada wild catch — supply is quota/stock-driven, not frost/heat or ENSO; wait for NOAA landings
_deliberately_absent.whole-trout / (Norway) salmon: North-Atlantic aquaculture — neither a subtropical land station nor ENSO is the honest driver
_deliberately_absent.beet (Canada 51%): temperate Canadian field crop — no acute frost-kill-at-origin signal the way subtropical produce has
_deliberately_absent.US-grown items: keep the existing USDM drought + NWS freeze machinery for domestic growing regions
